text: Now that Chapter 19 has explained them, what does each word in `public static void main(String[] args)` do?
choices: public: it is in the class's interface. static: it is compiled ahead of time. void: it has no side effects. String[]: the classpath entries.
public: it can be overridden. static: it runs first. void: it never throws. String[]: the environment variables.
public: the launcher can see it. static: no object need exist. void: nothing is returned to the JVM. String[]: the command-line arguments.
public: it is exported from the module. static: it is thread-safe. void: it returns via System.exit. String[]: the JVM flags.
explanation: Chapter 5 asked you to guess and Chapter 19 pays the debt. `static` is the load-bearing one: the launcher has a class name and nothing else, so a non-static method would require constructing an object, which would require choosing a constructor and having something to pass it. Nothing in the signature is decoration, and the exit status comes from `System.exit` rather than from a return value because `void` was chosen.
